external.reason: Ollama serves /api/chat at 127.0.0.1:11434; it is the inference runtime, not an artifact.
The torch 2.11.0+cu128 / transformers 5.16.1 environment only exists in this interpreter.
Generated code is executed in a throw-away directory; it is scoring scratch, never an input.
Only needed to REBUILD the corpus; the materialised jsonl in data/x3 is the training input.

experiment.name: d4
experiment.hypothesis: rebalancing the corpus to 1:1 repair:coding holds coding competence while keeping D3's repair gains, clearing the 106 baseline
experiment.single_variable: training data mix only: 132 repair + 132 contamination-screened coding replay rows, versus D3's 132 + 20; same parent, out_proj only, r4/a8, lr 1e-5, seed, 300 steps, ||delta|| 2.35 vs D3's 2.59

lane_audit.reason: lane served exactly the harness requests

experiment.why_not_promoted: below the baseline (102 vs 106) and the coding hypothesis is falsified: coding does not move (33, same as D3) and repair60 falls to 29; the first build scored 105 but was withdrawn because one row's instruction declared an eval entry point, and that single row (0.4% of the corpus) moved the score by 3 tasks
experiment.next_change: stop the adapter dose/mix search: six arms bracket 99-106 and a single training row moves the total by 3, so move to full-parameter continued pretraining on a corpus two orders of magnitude larger, or quantify test-time compute with the existing verifier

screen.name: d2
screen.kind: diagnostic screen (full lane deliberately not spent)
screen.why_not_promoted: screen is net negative (31/65 vs R5 33/65) with 7 collateral repair losses, so the full lane was not spent
screen.verdict: delta magnitude was a real limiter (5/7 targets recovered vs 2/7 for D1 at 15x the norm) but bounding it is not sufficient: a rank-4 update to six modules still trades seven repairs for five
screen.next_change: hold ||delta|| <= 3 as a constraint and change *which* weights move (attention-out only) or supervise paired same-problem/different-mutant contrast

repeat.protocol: greedy, temperature 0, seed 0, num_predict 768, same lane, same suite file; prompts hashed per task
repeat.supports: the harness itself is repeatable: the same weights and prompt give the same tokens and the same pass/fail vector, so a measured difference of one task is real measurement-wise. It does NOT mean arm comparisons are resolved to one task: D4 showed a single 736-token training row moves the suite by 3 tasks, so arm-to-arm claims need >3 tasks.
